mainTopic: When סימנים and serious wounds are enough to testify that a husband died
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining the argument about a mole: both sides may trust סימנים, and they argue only about whether a mole is a סימן מובהק. It then challenges the version of רבא that trusts סימנים מדאורייתא, since our משנה will not rely on signs on the body or belongings. The first answer is that body signs means weak ones like tall or short, and belongings may have been borrowed. The borrowing worry is tested against a donkey returned by its saddle and a lost גט tied to a ring, purse or money bag. The answer is that people do not lend these items. A second answer says the belongings had only common colors. Next the גמרא asks whether a person who is מגוייד can survive. אביי says our משנה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, and רבא says it is about a white-hot knife, which everyone agrees can save him. Finally, שמואל explains when a wild animal's bite or cutting both סימנים lets witnesses testify to death. The גמרא then works through challenges from giving a גט and from גלות.

steps.title: The argument is about whether a mole is a fully reliable sign
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends its answer: both sides agree סימנים count, and they only argue about whether a mole is a סימן מובהק.
steps.simpleTranslation: They argue about whether it is a clear, reliable sign. One Sage holds a mole is a clear sign, and the other Sage holds it is not a clear sign.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer about the argument over testifying based on a mole. It says the argument is only about how reliable a mole is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier it looked like the Sages were arguing about whether סימנים are trusted at all. Now the גמרא says both sides could hold סימנים are trusted, and the argument is narrower: is a mole a סימן מובהק? רבי אליעזר בן מהבאי says yes, so we may testify based on it. The first תנא says no.

keyTerms.meaning: A clear, highly reliable identifying sign
One Sage holds... and the other Sage holds

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer keeps the door open for the view that סימנים are trusted מדאורייתא. That view is the one the גמרא challenges next.

phrases.english: They are arguing about whether it is a clear sign.
phrases.notes: "It" is the mole (שומא) from the earlier ברייתא.

phrases.english: One Sage holds it is a clear sign,
and the other Sage holds it is not a clear sign.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer, begun before this section, explaining the argument over the mole.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the argument: it is about how reliable a mole is, not about whether סימנים count at all
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The Sages argue about whether סימנים are trusted מדאורייתא
steps.terutzMaskana: Both may agree סימנים count; they argue only about whether a mole is a סימן מובהק

steps.title: Challenge to רבא's version from our משנה
steps.stepSummary: If רבא holds סימנים are trusted מדאורייתא, why does the משנה say we do not rely on marks on the body and belongings?
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the version where רבא said סימנים are trusted by Torah law: but the משנה teaches, 'even though there are signs on his body and his belongings' we still do not rely on them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks one of the versions of רבא's opinion. It quotes our משנה, which seems to say סימנים are not trusted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One version of רבא says סימנים are trusted by Torah law. But the משנה says that to identify a dead man we need his face and nose, even if there are signs on his body and his clothing. That sounds like סימנים are not good enough, which contradicts רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Identifying signs are trusted by Torah law
But it teaches! (introduces a challenge from a source)
On his body and on his belongings

phrases.english: And according to that version
phrases.notes: There were two reports of what רבא said; this is the one where he trusts סימנים.

phrases.english: in which Rava said identifying signs are trusted by Torah law,
but it teaches in the mishna:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ סִימָנִין בְּגוּפוֹ וּבְכֵלָיו!
phrases.english: Even though there are signs on his body and his belongings!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְהַךְ לִישָּׁנָא דְּאָמַר רָבָא סִימָנִין דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא, הָא קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After saving the view that סימנים count, the גמרא tests it against the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The version of רבא that says סימנים are trusted מדאורייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה refuses to rely on signs on the body and belongings, which suggests סימנים are not trusted by Torah law

steps.title: Body marks means weak signs, and belongings may be borrowed
steps.stepSummary: The משנה only rejects weak body signs like tall or short, and belongings because they may have been borrowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'His body' means he was tall or short. 'His belongings' are not trusted because we worry they were borrowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining the משנה in a way that fits רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is not rejecting good סימנים. On the body, it means vague signs like height, which many people share. On belongings, the sign may be fine, but the clothing might have been borrowed from someone else, so it does not prove who the dead man is.
steps.confusionAlert: The problem with the belongings is not that the signs are weak. The signs may be strong, but they only prove whose item it is, not who was wearing it.

phrases.english: His body means that he was tall or short.
His belongings, because we are concerned about borrowing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the משנה: weak body signs, and a separate worry about borrowed items
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה rejects only vague body signs and belongings that may have been borrowed

steps.title: Then how do we return a donkey by its saddle marks?
steps.stepSummary: If we worry about borrowing, we should not return a lost donkey based on signs on its saddle.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we worry about borrowing, how do we return a donkey based on signs on its saddle?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the worry about borrowing, using a rule from returning lost objects.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A found donkey is given back to someone who describes signs on its saddle. But if things may be borrowed, the saddle could belong to the claimant while the donkey belongs to someone else. So the worry about borrowing seems to clash with that practice.

phrases.english: But if we are concerned about borrowing,
a donkey, by signs on the saddle,
how do we return it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the borrowing worry used in the last answer.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If items may be borrowed, a saddle's signs would not prove who owns the donkey, yet we return it

steps.title: People do not borrow saddles
steps.stepSummary: Saddles are not lent out because a saddle that does not fit hurts the donkey.
steps.simpleTranslation: People do not borrow a saddle, because it rubs the donkey sore.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the saddle case is different, because saddles are almost never borrowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A saddle is fitted to its own donkey. Someone else's saddle would rub and hurt the animal, so people don't borrow saddles. Because of this, the worry about borrowing does not apply, and the saddle's signs show who owns the donkey.

phrases.english: People do not borrow a saddle,
because it bruises the donkey.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the saddle challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual distinction: saddles are an exception to the borrowing worry
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Saddles may be borrowed like any other item
steps.terutzMaskana: Saddles are not borrowed, so their signs reliably show ownership

steps.title: A lost גט tied to a purse, bag or ring
steps.stepSummary: A found גט tied to a purse, money bag or ring is identified by them, but those could be borrowed too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he found it tied to a purse, a money bag or a ring, how can we return it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises another challenge to the borrowing worry, this time from the ברייתא about a lost גט. The next step answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says a lost גט found tied to a purse, money bag or ring may be delivered based on signs on those items. Those items are easy to lend, unlike a saddle. So if we worry about borrowing, how can we trust them to show whose גט it is?

phrases.english: If he found it tied to a purse,
phrases.notes: "It" is a lost גט, from the ברייתא quoted earlier.

phrases.english: or a money bag, or a ring,
how can we return it?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְצָאוֹ קָשׁוּר בְּכִיס וּבְאַרְנָקִי וּבְטַבַּעַת, הֵיכִי מַהְדְּרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the saddle is explained, the גמרא brings a case where the saddle answer does not work.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Purses, money bags and rings are easily lent, yet the ברייתא relies on them to return a lost גט

steps.title: Rings, purses and money bags are not lent out
steps.stepSummary: A ring is not lent because of fear of forgery, and a purse or money bag is not lent because people see lending them as a bad sign.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ring: people worry it will be used for forgery. A purse and a money bag: people treat lending them as a bad omen, so they do not lend them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 6. It explains why we may trust a ring, purse or money bag tied to a found גט even though belongings can be borrowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry about borrowing only applies to things people normally lend. A signet ring could be used to forge a signature, so its owner keeps it to himself. A purse or money bag is felt to be bad luck to lend. So these items, like the saddle, really do point to their owner.

keyTerms.meaning: ring (here, a signet ring used for sealing)
they treat it as a bad omen

phrases.english: A ring: people are worried about forgery.
phrases.notes: A ring used to stamp documents could be used to fake the owner's signature, so nobody lends it.

phrases.english: A purse and a money bag:
people see it as a bad omen and do not lend them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 6 about the גט tied to a purse, money bag or ring.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing case: these particular items are not normally lent out.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any belonging might be borrowed, so a ring, purse or money bag should not identify the owner of the גט.
steps.terutzMaskana: These specific items are not lent, so the borrowing worry does not apply to them.

steps.title: A second answer: the belongings in the משנה had only general colors
steps.stepSummary: Another way to explain the משנה: belongings are not trusted when the only sign is a general color like white or red.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say instead: 'his belongings' in the משנה means they were only identified by being white or red.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different answer to the original question about why the משנה does not trust signs on belongings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer said belongings might have been borrowed. This answer says the problem is the sign itself: white or red clothing is so common that it identifies nobody. A clear, specific mark on belongings would be trusted.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you want, say (introduces another answer)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה rejects weak, general signs. A ring, purse or money bag is trusted because people do not lend them. Another answer says the belongings in the משנה were only described by a common color.

phrases.english: And if you want, say: his belongings
phrases.notes: This goes back to the משנה's line that we do not trust signs on his belongings.

phrases.english: are only described as white or red.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the question of Step 2, as an alternative to the borrowing explanation in Step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the signs on the belongings were too general.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה rejects all signs on belongings.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה rejects only general signs such as a common color.

steps.title: Can a cut-open person really survive?
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה suggests a מגוייד person might live, but a משנה about טומאה implies he will not survive.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And even if they saw him cut open, and so on.' Does this mean a person who is cut open can live? But a different source teaches: A person does not make things impure until his soul leaves, even if he is cut open, and even if he is dying. This means he does not make things impure yet, but he is not going to live!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, which says we do not testify about a man seen מגוייד. It then points out that this seems to clash with another משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה will not let his wife remarry, so it treats a מגוייד as someone who might live. The משנה about טומאת מת says a מגוייד does not make things impure only because he has not died yet. That suggests his death is certain, so the two sources seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: and they pointed out a contradiction

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה about טומאה is not deciding whether he lives. It says he does not make things impure yet, and the גמרא reads this as implying he will certainly die.

phrases.english: The משנה said: "And even if they saw him cut open, etc."
Is this to say that a cut-open person can live?
But they pointed out a contradiction:

phrases.aramaic: אָדָם אֵינוֹ מְטַמֵּא עַד שֶׁתֵּצֵא נַפְשׁוֹ,
phrases.english: A person does not make things impure until his soul leaves,
even if he is cut open, and even if he is dying.
So he does not make things impure yet,
but as for living, he will not live!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by quoting the next clause of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that we do not testify that a מגוייד person has died.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Contradiction between sources: the משנה about טומאה implies a מגוייד will certainly die, so we should be able to testify about his death.

steps.title: אביי: the two sources follow different opinions
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, who says a מגוייד might survive. The משנה about טומאה follows the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is not difficult. This משנה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, and that one follows the רבנן. As a ברייתא teaches: We may testify about a person who is cut open, but not about a person who was crucified. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: Even about a cut-open person we do not testify, because the wound can be burned closed and he can live.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the contradiction by saying the two sources follow two different תנאים. He brings a ברייתא where they argue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the רבנן, a מגוייד will surely die, so witnesses may testify about his death, and the משנה about טומאה fits their view. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר holds that burning the wound closed can stop the bleeding and save him, so we do not testify. Our משנה follows him.

keyTerms.meaning: to have the wound burned closed

phrases.english: Abaye said: It is not difficult:

phrases.aramaic: הָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר, הָא רַבָּנַן,
phrases.english: this follows Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar, and that follows the Rabbis,
phrases.notes: "This" is our משנה, and "that" is the משנה about impurity.

phrases.english: as it is taught:
We may testify about a cut-open person,
but we may not testify about a crucified person.
Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
Even about a cut-open person we do not testify,
because his wound can be burned closed and he can live.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the sources to different תנאים (a מחלוקת).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources share one view about whether a מגוייד can survive.
steps.terutzMaskana: Our משנה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, and the משנה about טומאה follows the רבנן.

steps.title: The incident in עסיא seems to go against רבי שמעון בן אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: The end of our משנה lets the wife remarry when the leg was cut off above the knee. That seems to treat a serious wound as certain death, unlike רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But can you really say our משנה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר? The end of the משנה teaches: There was an incident in עסיא with a man they lowered into the sea, and only his leg came up in their hands. The חכמים said: If it was cut from the knee and above, his wife may marry. If it was cut from the knee and below, she may not marry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי's answer. It quotes the end of our own משנה, which seems to disagree with רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the עסיא case the wife may remarry when the leg was cut off above the knee, so the משנה assumes a wound like that kills. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר said that even a מגוייד might survive if the wound is burned closed. So how can the same משנה follow his view?

keyTerms.meaning: you can explain it as following
the end part of the משנה
they lowered him on a rope

phrases.aramaic: וּמִי מָצֵית לְאוֹקוֹמֵי כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר?
phrases.english: But can you explain it as following Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar?
But the end of the משנה teaches:
There was an incident in Asya
with a man whom they lowered into the sea,
and only his leg came up in their hands,
and the Sages said:
If it was cut from the knee and above, she may marry,
phrases.notes: "She" is his wife. The cut is on the leg that came up.

phrases.english: if from the knee and below, she may not marry.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי מָצֵית לְאוֹקוֹמֵי כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אביי's answer in Step 10 using the end of the same משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that our משנה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Internal inconsistency: the end of the משנה treats a severe wound (leg cut above the knee) as certain death, which contradicts רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's concern that the wound could be burned closed and the man could live.

steps.title: Water makes a wound worse
steps.stepSummary: The case that allows testimony involved water, and water makes a wound deadly. So even רבי שמעון בן אלעזר would agree that the man died.
steps.simpleTranslation: Water is different, because it makes the wound worse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 11. That case is special because the wounded man was in water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says a serious wound alone does not prove death. Here, though, water was added to the wound, and water makes the wound much worse. So in that case death is certain even according to him, and our משנה can still follow his view.

phrases.english: Water is different,
because it makes the wound worse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: an extra factor (water) is present.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The end of the משנה seemed to treat a wound by itself as certain death, which goes against רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.terutzMaskana: Death there is certain only because water made the wound worse. Our משנה can still follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.

steps.title: The camel that died before it stopped crying out
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה saw an Arab cut open his camel, and it died at once. This suggests that a living thing that is cut open cannot survive.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבה בר בר חנה say: I myself saw an Arab who took a sword and cut open his camel, and the camel died before it could even stop its cry?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that a מגוייד person might live. It brings an eyewitness story of a camel that died right away after being cut open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a camel died so fast, a person who is cut open should also be counted as dead for sure. That goes against רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, and against our משנה, which follows him.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabba bar bar Chana say:
I myself saw
a certain Arab who took a sword
and cut open his camel,
and it did not even stop its braying!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a new challenge against the claim that a מגוייד might survive.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, which our משנה follows, that a מגוייד may survive.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An eyewitness saw a cut-open camel die instantly. So being cut open should mean certain death.

steps.title: That camel was weak
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the camel was thin and weak, so it died quickly. A healthy creature might survive.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: That camel was weak.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the camel story. That camel was already weak, so the story proves nothing about a healthy body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The camel died at once because it had no strength, not because every cut-open creature dies. So the view that a מגוייד might live still stands.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
That one was weak.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the camel challenge in Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the proof: that case was unusual.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The camel's instant death seemed to show that any cut-open creature dies.
steps.terutzMaskana: That camel was weak. A healthy body cut open might survive.

steps.title: A white-hot knife, and everyone agrees
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different answer to the contradiction between our משנה and the משנה about טומאה. Our משנה is about someone cut with a white-hot knife, and in that case everyone agrees he might live.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Our משנה is talking about a white-hot knife, and it is the opinion of everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a new way to settle the contradiction from Step 9. He does not need to say that our משנה follows only רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A white-hot knife burns the wound shut as it cuts, so the person might survive. Because of that, even the רבנן agree that we may not testify that he died. The משנה about טומאה is about an ordinary cut, where he will die.

keyTerms.meaning: אמורא who gives a different answer

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not answering the camel story. He is giving a whole new answer to the contradiction in Step 9, replacing the approach that the two משניות follow different תנאים.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Our משנה is talking about a white-hot knife,
phrases.notes: The heat seals the wound shut, which is why the man might live.

phrases.english: and it is the opinion of everyone.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: בְּסַכִּין מְלוּבֶּנֶת, וְדִבְרֵי הַכֹּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the contradiction raised in Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case so that both משניות fit everyone's view.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two משניות seemed to disagree, so we said they follow different תנאים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Our משנה is about a white-hot knife, where survival is possible according to all. The other משנה is about an ordinary cut.
steps.whyThisMatters: With this answer, our משנה no longer depends on a minority view. It fits everyone's opinion.

steps.title: Which bites by a wild animal count as deadly
steps.stepSummary: שמואל limits the משנה's case of a wild animal eating a person. We may not testify only when the animal eats a part that does not cause death. If it eats a part that does cause death, we may testify.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: "Or a wild animal was eating him." רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: They taught this only when it ate from a place where his life does not leave. But if it ate from a place where his life leaves, we may testify that he died.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next case in the משנה, the wild animal. רב יהודה quotes שמואל to explain exactly when this case applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that if you saw an animal eating someone, you may not testify that he died. שמואל says this is only true when the animal ate a part like a hand or foot, which does not kill. If it ate a part that surely causes death, we may testify.

keyTerms.meaning: they only taught (this) in the case of

steps.whatToRemember: A wild animal eating someone does not prove death unless it ate a part of the body that surely causes death.

phrases.english: "Or a wild animal was eating him," etc.
Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
They taught this only
when it ate from a place where his life does not leave,
but if it ate from a place where his life leaves —
we may testify.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the מגוייד discussion to the next case in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's ruling that we may not testify applies only when the animal ate a part that does not cause death. If it ate a part that surely causes death, we may testify.

steps.title: Testifying after both passageways were cut
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that if a man's two סימנים, or most of them, were cut and he ran off, we may testify that he died.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: if someone cut a man's two passageways, or most of the two, and the man ran away, witnesses may testify that he died.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ruling of שמואל, right after his rule about a wild animal. It says a man whose two סימנים were cut is treated as surely dead, even if nobody saw him die.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The witnesses did not see the death itself. They only saw the cut and saw the man run away. שמואל says this wound is so certain to kill that their testimony is enough to let his wife remarry.

keyTerms.meaning: The two סימנים: the windpipe and the food pipe
Most of the way through each of the two passageways

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
If someone cut his two [passageways],
phrases.notes: The "two" are the windpipe and the food pipe, the same two cuts made in שחיטה.

phrases.english: or most of the two,
and he ran away, we may testify [that he died].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ruling of שמואל that also defines which wounds count as surely deadly for testimony.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cutting both סימנים, or most of both, counts as a deadly wound. Witnesses may testify that the man died even though he ran away.

steps.title: A man with cut passageways can still order a divorce
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל from another ruling of his: such a man can still order a גט, which means he counts as alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But didn't רב יהודה say in the name of שמואל: if someone cut a man's two passageways, or most of them, and the man gestured, "Write a גט for my wife," then the people there should write it and give it to her?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question. שמואל himself said such a man can still divorce his wife, so how can we treat him as dead?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a living husband can divorce his wife. If the cut man can still order a גט, he must count as alive. That seems to clash with the earlier ruling that we testify he is dead.

keyTerms.meaning: They should write it and give it

steps.confusionAlert: Both rulings come from the same speakers, רב יהודה in the name of שמואל. The question is not a disagreement between two people. It is a seeming contradiction inside שמואל's own rulings.

phrases.english: Is that so?
But didn't Rav Yehuda say that Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁחַט בּוֹ שְׁנַיִם אוֹ רוֹב שְׁנַיִם,
phrases.english: If someone cut his two [passageways] or most of the two,
and he gestured and said:
"Write a bill of divorce for my wife,"
then these [people] should write it and give it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 17 with a contradicting ruling of the same אמורא.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that we testify the man died
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If he can give a גט, he is legally alive. So how can we testify that he is dead?

steps.title: Alive now, but sure to die
steps.stepSummary: The man is alive for now, so he can give a גט, but he will certainly die, so we can testify later.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is alive right now, but in the end he will die.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that both rulings are true, because they are about two different moments in time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While he is still breathing he is a living husband, so his גט works. Since the wound will surely kill him, after a while witnesses may say he has died. One ruling is about now, and the other is about the end result.

keyTerms.meaning: And he will end up dying

phrases.english: He is alive [now],
but in the end he will die.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting by time: alive for now, dead in the end
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Being able to give a גט means the wound might not be deadly.
steps.terutzMaskana: He is alive for now, so the גט works, but his death is certain, so testimony is allowed.

steps.title: Then the one who cut him should go to exile
steps.stepSummary: If the wound is surely deadly, the one who cut him by accident should go to גלות, but a ברייתא says he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, the one who cut him should be sent to גלות because of him. Why was it taught in a ברייתא: if someone cut a man's two passageways, or most of the two, he is not sent to גלות?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question that comes from the last answer. If death is certain, the one who caused it by accident should be treated as a killer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who kills by accident must go to גלות in an עיר מקלט. If cutting the סימנים is a sure death, the cutter is the killer and should go to גלות. The ברייתא says he does not, which suggests the wound is not considered surely deadly.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so (opens a challenge built on the last answer)
Goes to exile, the punishment for killing by accident
Why was it taught (in a ברייתא)?

phrases.english: But if so,
let [the one who cut him] go to exile because of him.
phrases.notes: Someone who kills by accident runs to an עיר מקלט. That is גלות.

phrases.english: Why was it taught:
If he cut the two or most of the two
he does not go to exile!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, יְהֵא גּוֹלֶה עַל יָדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 19's claim that death is certain, and challenges it from the laws of גלות.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a man with cut סימנים will surely die
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A sure death would make the cutter a killer who must go to גלות. The ברייתא says he is exempt.

steps.title: Maybe the wind made it worse
steps.stepSummary: רב הושעיא explains that the cutter is exempt from גלות because the wind may have sped up the death.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was already said about that ברייתא: רב הושעיא said, we are concerned that perhaps the wind upset his condition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by quoting רב הושעיא's explanation of the ברייתא. The man surely dies, but the cutter is not the only possible cause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Death is still certain, so testimony stays allowed. For גלות, though, the cutter must be the one who caused the death. Since the wind may have played a part, we cannot fully blame him.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was already said about it
Upset him, made his condition worse

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that "he will surely die" and "you are the one who killed him" are two separate questions. That is how the two rulings can both stand.

phrases.english: But it was said about it,
Rav Hoshaya said:
We are concerned that perhaps
the wind made his condition worse.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא אִיתְּמַר עֲלַהּ, אָמַר רַב הוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from גלות in step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Separating certain death from who caused the death
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Being exempt from גלות means the wound is not surely deadly.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wound is surely deadly, but the wind may have sped up the death, so the cutter is not fully the killer.

steps.title: A second reason begins: maybe the man himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a second reason why the cutter is exempt from גלות, pointing to the wounded man himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Alternatively, perhaps he himself...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a second answer to the גלות question. The sentence is cut off here and continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the first answer, this one will suggest another cause of death besides the cutter. This time the cause is something about the wounded man himself. The rest of the idea comes in the next lines.

phrases.english: Alternatively, perhaps he himself...
phrases.notes: "He" is the wounded man. The sentence finishes in the next lines of the גמרא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer, alongside רב הושעיא's, to the challenge in step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A second possible cause of death, coming from the wounded man himself
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the wind could explain the exemption from גלות.
steps.terutzMaskana: The answer is completed in the following lines.
